metadata.title: Hypervelocity Stars: From the Galactic Center to the Halo

evidence.quote:
The star, SDSS
J090745.0+024507, is leaving the Galaxy

In 2005, Brown et al. (2005) reported the first discovery of a HVS. The star, SDSS
J090745.0+024507, is leaving the Galaxy
The star, SDSS J090745.0+024507, is leaving the Galaxy with a heliocentric radial velocity of8 5 3 { \pm } 1 2 \mathrm { k m } \mathrm { s } ^ { - 1 }

notes: Only one star is individually designated and explicitly described as leaving the Galaxy: SDSS J090745.0+024507 (T:p3-b0). It is classified as follow_up because the paper attributes its discovery and HVS status to Brown et al. (2005). Other HVS detections are given only as unnamed descriptive samples or group counts, such as the additional seven HVSs whose velocities are said to exceed the escape velocity (T:p3-b2), so they cannot be separated into individual star entries. The model populations in the tables and figures are synthetic mass bins rather than individual stars.
